components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default CTA — black fill, white text. Inverts to slightly lighter black on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 40px; padding: 0 18px; background: #222222; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-family: 'Inter Tight', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; color: #FFFFFF; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #3A3A38; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #222222; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Ghost variant — transparent with black stroke. Inverts to solid black on hover, converging with primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 40px; padding: 0 18px; background: transparent; border: 1.5px solid #222222; border-radius: 8px; font-family: 'Inter Tight', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; color: #222222; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #222222; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #222222; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Kicker Label
components.description: Uppercase eyebrow label placed above a section title. Establishes context; never used decoratively.
components.css: .ds-kicker { display: block; font-family: 'Inter Tight', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6F6F68; margin-bottom: 12px; }

narrative.overview:
ToolTrim's visual system is built around one conviction: the design should disappear so the judgment can speak. Not minimalism as aesthetic posture, but minimalism as discipline — every element that isn't load-bearing gets removed. The result is a surface that feels neither cold nor warm, but exact. Like a well-annotated page in a technical report: nothing decorative, everything purposeful.

The palette is essentially achromatic. Warm near-black text on a warm off-white ground, depth achieved entirely through tonal layering rather than shadow or color contrast. Three surface tones (#F8F8F4 → #F1F1EC → #FFFFFF) create hierarchy without noise. The single blue carried in the codebase is a technical residual — not a design choice, not a brand signal. This system trusts monochrome completely.

Typography does all the expressive work. Uncut Sans at extreme scale and tight tracking (-0.07em) creates authority at the display level. Inter Tight handles everything else — lean, functional, legible at 16px. The gap between display and body is large by design: hierarchy by contrast, not by color.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic in practice: black, warm grey, off-white
Tonal depth with zero box-shadow on content surfaces
Uncut Sans for display scale only; Inter Tight owns all content
Borders as section markers, not decoration
No gradients, no blurs, no glass effects, no badge multiplication

rules.name: The Monochrome Commitment Rule
rules.body: This system has no accent color. The blue in the codebase is a technical residual being phased out. Do not introduce new color to fill the void; the void is the point.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: Depth is encoded in three surface steps: bg (#F8F8F4) → surface-soft (#F1F1EC) → white (#FFFFFF). Use this stack to communicate hierarchy — do not reach for shadow or color to do the same job.

rules.name: The Display Monopoly Rule
rules.body: Uncut Sans is used exclusively at display scale (44px and above). It never appears at body size. Inter Tight owns everything under 26px.

rules.name: The Tight-Track Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing decreases as text grows: display uses -0.07em, body uses -0.01 to -0.02em, labels use +0.08em (uppercase only). Never apply positive tracking to lowercase text.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content surfaces are always flat. Borders — not shadows — define card boundaries. If you're tempted to add box-shadow to a card, use a border: 1px solid #DADAD4 instead.

rules.name: The Float-Signals-Detachment Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element has left the document flow. If it hasn't left the flow, it doesn't get a shadow.

dos: Do use tonal layering (surface-soft → white) to create depth — the only elevation tool for content surfaces.
Do use border: 1px solid #DADAD4 as the canonical card boundary.
Do keep Uncut Sans exclusively at display scale (44px and above).
Do let whitespace vary deliberately — tighter within a section, generous between sections.
Do lead every verdict section with the decision itself. Judgment precedes rationale.
Do use the tt-kicker pattern (uppercase, +0.08em, #6F6F68) as the singular metadata label above headings.
Do write border-bottom: 1px solid #DADAD4 as section separators.
donts: Don't add box-shadow to inline cards or content panels.
Don't use border-left thicker than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't create badge proliferation — star ratings, upvote counts, affiliate signals (G2/Capterra patterns).
Don't use the blue accent (#1E4FCC) for decorative purposes — it is a residual being phased out.
Don't use pastel fills, emojis in UI, or gamification cues (Product Hunt patterns).
Don't add three-column feature grids with icon + heading + text (SaaS landing page cliché).
Don't repeat CTAs at every scroll position.
Don't apply glassmorphism or blur-based layering — no backdrop-filter.
Don't use identical padding everywhere — rhythm requires variation.
